topics.title: UK homes are offered help for solar panels and heat pumps
topics.summary: The UK is preparing low- or no-interest Warm Home Loans to help households pay for solar panels and heat pumps. The plan aims to reduce upfront costs and lower future energy bills.
topics.discussionPrompt: If you could upgrade one thing at home to make life easier or cheaper, would it be better insulation, solar power, a smarter thermostat, a new appliance, or something else?

topics.title: Sardinian restaurants try screen-free family meals
topics.summary: Fifteen restaurants in Sardinia are piloting a screen-free dining program for families. Phones are put away and children receive games and conversation activities intended to make mealtimes more social.
topics.discussionPrompt: Could you enjoy a phone-free meal, or would it feel strange? What would make the table more fun: games, conversation cards, music, drawing, or a really good dessert?

topics.title: A handwritten Rolling Stones letter heads to auction
topics.summary: A 1962 letter from Brian Jones asking Charlie Watts to join his young band will be auctioned in New York. The document captures the early days before the Rolling Stones’ classic lineup came together.
topics.discussionPrompt: What tiny piece of music history would you love to own: an early handwritten lyric, a concert poster, a first pressing, a backstage photo, or an instrument pick?

topics.title: Ancient landscapes help explain Venice’s lagoon
topics.summary: Scientists have mapped ancient hills and swamps beneath the northern Adriatic, showing how rising seas gradually transformed dry land into the Venice lagoon over thousands of years.
topics.discussionPrompt: If you could see your region thousands of years ago, what would surprise you most: the shoreline, forests, animals, rivers, glaciers, or where people once lived?

topics.title: China’s coastal wetlands turn a vivid red
topics.summary: Autumn seepweed has turned wetlands near Qingdao, China, a striking crimson. The seasonal color change creates a red-beach mosaic across salt marshes from September through November.
topics.discussionPrompt: What seasonal change do you look forward to seeing most: autumn colors, the first snow, spring blossoms, summer storms, migrating birds, or something local?

topics.title: Gulliver’s Travels reaches its 300th anniversary
topics.summary: Ireland is marking 300 years since Jonathan Swift’s Gulliver’s Travels was published. Exhibitions, talks, and performances are exploring how its satire still speaks to modern readers.
topics.discussionPrompt: Which old book, movie, or song still feels surprisingly modern to you? Is it the story, the humor, the characters, or the questions it asks?

topics.title: A rare dinosaur skeleton sells for $47.3 million
topics.summary: A Nanotyrannus skeleton named Jodi sold at a New York auction for $47.3 million. Sotheby’s called it the second most valuable dinosaur fossil ever sold at auction.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a museum could borrow one extraordinary object for your town, would you choose a dinosaur fossil, moon rock, famous painting, vintage train, or a historical treasure?

topics.title: HSBC reports a stronger quarter
topics.summary: HSBC reported a 32% rise in quarterly profits while saying it faces no pressure to move its headquarters from the UK. The results feed into continuing discussion about bank taxes and consumer affordability.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a big company has a strong year, where should its extra money go first: lower prices, better service, staff pay, new ideas, taxes, or investor returns?

topics.title: Emergency-planning advice changes shopping lists
topics.summary: UK retailers reported increased sales of bottled water, tinned food, wind-up radios, and torches after government guidance encouraged households to prepare for disruptions from extreme weather or cyber incidents.
topics.discussionPrompt: What three practical items would you keep for a short power outage or stormy weekend: snacks, flashlight, radio, blankets, board games, phone battery, or something else?

topics.title: Commonwealth leaders will discuss slavery’s legacy
topics.summary: King Charles said he will discuss the legacy of slavery with Commonwealth leaders during a Caribbean summit. The visit has renewed attention on historical acknowledgment, dialogue, and calls for reparative action.
topics.discussionPrompt: When communities reckon with difficult history, what helps a conversation stay thoughtful: listening first, learning local stories, public art, school lessons, shared events, or something else?
